name: Arrays & Strings
intro: Contiguous data and indices. Patterns are listed in the order worth learning them — each one builds on the previous.

patterns.name: Traversal & simulation
patterns.when: Just walk the array / string once and track something.
patterns.explain: One loop, a few variables (count, max, current streak…). The foundation every other pattern builds on.

patterns.name: In-place modification
patterns.when: Rearrange or overwrite without extra memory.
patterns.explain: Use a write index (or swaps) to rebuild the array inside itself, in `O(1)` extra space.

patterns.name: Sorting first
patterns.when: Order makes the problem easier (duplicates, anagrams, intervals).
patterns.explain: `sort()` once in `O(n log n)`, then a simple pass solves what was hard on unsorted data.

patterns.name: Prefix sum
patterns.when: Many range-sum queries on a fixed array.
patterns.explain: Precompute `pre[i] = a[0] + … + a[i-1]`; any range sum becomes `pre[r] - pre[l]`.

patterns.name: Hashing
patterns.when: Fast lookup or counting of things already seen.
patterns.explain: `unordered_map` / `unordered_set` (or a `count[26]` array for letters) make each lookup `O(1)` instead of rescanning.

patterns.name: Two pointers
patterns.when: Sorted input, or comparing from both ends.
patterns.explain: Two indices move toward each other (or one chases the other) based on a condition. No extra memory.

patterns.name: Sliding window
patterns.explain: Keep a window `[left, right]` and update the answer as it slides, instead of re-checking every subarray.
